title: Born of the wind's blessing
story: Anjana and Kesari prayed for a child. In the tradition, Vayu, the wind god, played a part in the birth, which is why Hanuman is called Pavanputra, son of the wind.
hit: Where you start doesn't set your ceiling.
image_scene: Baby Hanuman floating on soft wind swirls above a quiet forest hill, parents' silhouettes below.

title: His name means 'jaw'
story: Hanu means jaw. The name comes from a childhood injury, when a blow left his jaw marked. One scar gave him the name the whole world now says.
hit: Your hardest day can end up as your name.
image_scene: Baby Hanuman touching his chin with a small surprised smile, golden light around him.

title: He tried to eat the sun
story: Baby Hanuman saw the rising sun, thought it was a glowing fruit, and leapt into the sky to grab it. The gods watched a toddler race the sun.
hit: Big dreams look silly right up until they don't.
image_scene: Baby Hanuman mid-leap toward a huge orange sun, clouds below, arms stretched out.

title: Rahu's complaint
story: Rahu was about to swallow the sun for an eclipse when a little monkey zoomed past and pushed him aside. He ran to Indra, the king of the gods, to complain.
hit: Some people disrupt the system just by arriving.
image_scene: Dark Rahu shadow figure looking shocked as baby Hanuman zooms past toward the sun.

title: When the wind stopped
story: Indra struck Hanuman with his thunderbolt and he fell. Vayu, heartbroken, pulled all air out of the world. Every creature struggled until the gods begged him to return.
hit: A parent's hurt can pause the whole world.
image_scene: Father wind god cradling baby Hanuman, swirling pale air gathering into his hands, trees still.

title: A starter pack from the gods
story: To make peace, the gods gave gifts. Brahma, Indra, Varuna and others blessed him with strength, a body that could take hits, and protection from many weapons.
hit: Great things are built by lots of people backing you.
image_scene: Baby Hanuman surrounded by glowing gift orbs from several gods, each a different soft colour.

title: Why fire couldn't hurt him
story: Agni, the fire god, blessed Hanuman so that flames would not harm him. Many years later that boon would matter more than anyone expected, in a city called Lanka.
hit: Prep now for a problem you can't see yet.
image_scene: Baby Hanuman sitting calmly in a ring of gentle orange flames, smiling.

title: The curse that made him forget
story: Young Hanuman played pranks on sages who were meditating. They cursed him, gently: he would forget his own powers until someone reminded him. That reminder came years later.
hit: Imposter syndrome is older than the Ramayana.
image_scene: Hanuman looking at his own reflection in a pond, puzzled, tiny sparkles fading from his hands.

title: The student who faced the sun
story: Hanuman asked Surya, the sun god, to teach him. Surya never stops moving, so Hanuman followed him across the sky, walking backwards, eyes on his teacher.
hit: Commitment looks like showing up facing forward.
image_scene: Hanuman flying backwards across an orange sky, facing a smiling sun with book scrolls.

title: His fee: serve a friend
story: When his studies ended, Surya asked for no money. His fee was that Hanuman would serve and protect Sugriva, Surya's son. That promise led Hanuman straight to Ram.
hit: The best 'payment' for knowledge is how you use it for others.
image_scene: Hanuman bowing to Surya in golden light, a small vanara prince watching nearby.

title: One person, many names
story: Anjaneya, Maruti, Pavanputra, Kesarinandan, Bajrangbali, Mahavir, Sankat Mochan. Each name is a different side of him. Which one feels like yours?
hit: You are allowed to be more than one thing.
image_scene: Baby Hanuman with seven floating name-scrolls in soft calligraphy circling around him.

title: The gods' team-up
story: When Vishnu was to come as Ram, many gods took vanara forms to help him. Hanuman is counted among them, with Vayu in his story and, in some traditions, a link to Shiva.
hit: The best teams are put together before the mission begins.
image_scene: A circle of small glowing vanara cubs, one with a topknot at centre, golden sparks overhead.

title: He is still here
story: Hanuman is called a chiranjivi, one who lives on. Tradition says he stays on earth as long as Ram's name is spoken. Every chant is a kind of invitation.
hit: Some things stay alive because people keep showing up.
image_scene: Hanuman meditating peacefully on a mountain at dusk with floating lanterns.

title: Where was he born?
story: Several places say it happened here: Anjanadri near Hampi in Karnataka, a hill in Jharkhand, Tirumala in Andhra and more. Devotees have never agreed on one spot.
hit: Some stories are big enough for many homes.
image_scene: A map-like collage of small hills, each with a tiny temple and a different-colored banner.

title: The disguise that didn't last
story: Sugriva sent Hanuman, dressed as a simple brahmin, to find out who the two warriors in the forest were. One conversation with Ram and he knew exactly who he was talking to.
hit: Real recognise real.
image_scene: Hanuman as a young brahmin with a staff meeting Ram and Lakshman on a forest path.

title: 'Who speaks this well?'
story: In the Valmiki Ramayana, after hearing Hanuman speak, Ram turns to Lakshman and says only someone who has studied deeply could talk like this. First impression, by speech.
hit: Clear words are a superpower.
image_scene: Ram and Lakshman listening in awe as Hanuman speaks with gentle hand gestures.

title: He carried them both
story: The vanaras' mountain home was hard to climb, so Hanuman lifted Ram and Lakshman onto his shoulders and carried them up to meet Sugriva. Effort without ego.
hit: Show up for people. Do the carrying.
image_scene: Hanuman climbing a rocky path with Ram and Lakshman seated on his shoulders, grinning.

title: The original wingman
story: Hanuman brought Ram and Sugriva together. Each had a problem the other could solve: Ram needed help finding Sita, and Sugriva had lost his kingdom. A fire witnessed their friendship.
hit: Introductions can change history.
image_scene: Ram and Sugriva shaking hands beside a sacred fire while Hanuman stands between them, smiling.

title: Why Ram gave him the ring
story: Before sending the search parties, Ram gave Hanuman his signet ring to show Sita. Of everyone there, he trusted Hanuman with the one thing that proved the message was real.
hit: Be the person others hand their important thing to.
image_scene: Ram placing a small gold ring in Hanuman's open palm, soft glow between them.

title: Service as a love language
story: Hanuman's devotion is called dasya bhakti, love through service. He never asks for a title. He asks what needs doing and gets on with it.
hit: Showing love can be as simple as being useful.
image_scene: Hanuman kneeling with folded hands, a broom, a water pot and a lantern beside him.

title: He never asked for a reward
story: After the war, Ram offered Hanuman any boon. He asked to keep devotion to Ram, and to stay as long as Ram's story is told. That was the whole ask.
hit: Rare people want only the thing itself.
image_scene: Ram offering a jewelled box, Hanuman gently shaking his head with a peaceful smile.

title: The seat that stays empty
story: Folk tradition says wherever the Ramayana is told, Hanuman comes to listen, invisibly, sitting with folded hands. Some storytellers still leave a seat for him.
hit: Real fans show up quietly.
image_scene: A glowing empty cushion at the front of a story circle, subtle golden shimmer above it.

title: A name that floats stones
story: To cross the sea to Lanka, the vanaras built a bridge. A folk story says stones with Ram's name written on them floated. Faith did the engineering.
hit: Belief can be the first load-bearing beam.
image_scene: Vanaras laying stones marked with 'Ram' in an arching bridge over sparkling ocean waves.

title: The giant in a tiny frame
story: Hanuman could grow as big as a mountain or shrink small enough to hide. The tradition calls these powers anima and mahima. The skill is knowing which size fits the room.
hit: Read the room. Resize.
image_scene: Hanuman shown twice in one frame: tiny on a leaf and huge behind it as a mountain.

title: Deadline missed, panic on
story: The search party reached the southern shore with no sign of Sita and a deadline already gone. They sat together, ready to give up. Then an old vulture, Sampati, pointed to Lanka.
hit: Panic is loud. Clarity arrives quietly.
image_scene: A group of tired vanaras on a beach at dusk, an old vulture on a rock pointing across the sea.

title: Nobody knew who could jump
story: Each vanara listed how far he could leap. Angada said he could get there but wasn't sure he'd get back. Everyone stared at the ocean, doing the math.
hit: Naming your limit honestly is leadership.
image_scene: Vanaras standing in a line at the shore, each holding up a different number of fingers.

title: Jambavan's pep talk
story: Old Jambavan walked over to the quiet one in the corner and said: you were born with this. Remember who you are. Hanuman remembered, and the curse of forgetting lifted.
hit: The right mentor reminds you what you forgot.
image_scene: Elderly bear Jambavan placing a hand on Hanuman's shoulder, golden light rising from Hanuman.

title: He grew until the mountain shook
story: On Mahendra mountain, Hanuman expanded to a giant size, stamped his feet and made the whole hill tremble. Then he flew. No hype video needed.
hit: Sometimes the preparation is the dramatic bit.
image_scene: Huge Hanuman crouching on a mountain peak preparing to leap, birds scattering below.

title: The polite no to rest
story: Mid-ocean, the mountain Mainaka rose from the sea offering Hanuman a rest. He touched it respectfully, thanked it, and kept flying. Rest is fine. Today, he had a promise.
hit: Say no kindly. Keep your goal.
image_scene: Hanuman lightly touching a green island that has risen from the sea, then flying onward.

title: Surasa's test
story: A sea-goddess named Surasa opened a huge mouth to test him. Hanuman got bigger, then suddenly tiny, slipped in and out, and thanked her. He passed without a fight.
hit: Winning sometimes means being flexible, not louder.
image_scene: Hanuman as a tiny figure flying out of a giant open-mouthed sea goddess's smile, waves around.

title: Simhika the shadow-catcher
story: A sea monster, Simhika, caught flyers by grabbing their shadows. Hanuman felt himself being dragged down, found the cause, and ended it from inside her.
hit: Some pulls come from what's hidden below.
image_scene: Hanuman flying above waves while a dark shadow shape clings to his own shadow on the water.

title: Cat-sized on Lanka's hill
story: He landed on a hill outside Lanka, saw the gold city and knew a giant vanara would be caught instantly. So he shrank to the size of a cat and slipped in at dusk.
hit: The best entrance is sometimes a small one.
image_scene: Tiny Hanuman the size of a cat walking along a golden city wall at sunset.

title: Lankini and the prophecy
story: The city's guardian, Lankini, spotted him and blocked the gate. Hanuman struck her once with his left hand. She bowed: Brahma had said that when a vanara beat her, Lanka's end had begun.
hit: Some doors open only after you win the first fight.
image_scene: Hanuman at a gleaming Lanka gate facing a tall female guardian who is lowering her weapon.

title: Searching every palace
story: He searched Ravana's palaces room by room. Seeing sleeping women, he questioned his own mind. 'It stayed pure,' he reflected. 'My mind remained steady.' He kept looking.
hit: Integrity is what you do when nobody's watching.
image_scene: Tiny Hanuman looking carefully through carved palace windows in lamplight, hand on his heart.

title: The wrong woman, the right call
story: In a grand palace he saw a beautiful queen and wondered for a moment if she was Sita. Then he reasoned: Sita would never sleep in luxury, away from Ram. He dropped the guess and kept searching instead of reporting a false win.
hit: Don't fake the result just to be done.
image_scene: Tiny Hanuman on a palace pillar looking at a sleeping queen, a thought bubble with a question mark.

title: Under the Ashoka tree
story: In a grove of Ashoka trees he found Sita: thin, quiet, guarded by demonesses. She had been waiting a long time for any sign that Ram was still looking.
hit: Hope often looks fragile and stays alive anyway.
image_scene: Hanuman hidden among leaves of a tall tree looking down at a calm Sita seated in a garden.

title: He waited, then spoke softly
story: Hanuman watched Ravana threaten Sita and wanted to act. He stayed hidden and thought it through. Then he began quietly telling Ram's story from the tree, so she wouldn't be frightened.
hit: Plan the first sentence. It decides the whole talk.
image_scene: Night garden, Hanuman perched on a branch whispering softly while Sita looks up in surprise.

title: Proof in a ring
story: Sita wondered if this was a trick. Hanuman handed her Ram's ring. She recognised it, cried, and believed him. Then she asked how one little vanara had crossed an ocean.
hit: Trust is built with details only the real person would know.
image_scene: Hanuman holding out a small golden ring to Sita under a tree, her hand reaching for it.

title: Sita said no to a ride home
story: Hanuman offered to carry Sita back to Ram right then. She declined, saying Ram should come and rescue her, and a rescue in the dark could put them both at risk. He accepted it.
hit: Respect someone's choice even when you can fix it faster.
image_scene: Hanuman bowing slightly with palms joined, Sita shaking her head gently with a calm smile.

title: A jewel for Ram
story: Before leaving, Sita gave Hanuman her chudamani, a hair jewel, to show Ram. It meant: she was alive, brave, and still waiting. He wrapped it carefully.
hit: Proof of life is a very small object sometimes.
image_scene: Sita handing a small glowing jewel to Hanuman who receives it with both hands.

title: Strategic garden chaos
story: Hanuman then ate fruit from Ravana's garden and uprooted trees. He wanted to be noticed, to see the enemy's strength, and learn the city before leaving. It was a plan, not a tantrum.
hit: Sometimes you cause a ripple to see who shows up.
image_scene: Hanuman happily holding a fruit and a small uprooted tree in a messy garden, guards running.

title: Akshay's last fight
story: Ravana sent his young son Akshayakumar to stop the intruder. Hanuman fought him fairly and ended it. Ravana's court started to realise this was no ordinary monkey.
hit: Underestimating someone is how stories turn.
image_scene: Hanuman standing calm in a garden with a broken chariot behind him, flames of battle sparks.

title: Caught on purpose
story: Indrajit used the Brahmastra, which Hanuman could have resisted. He chose to respect it and let himself be tied. He wanted to meet Ravana in person.
hit: A planned surrender can be a smart move.
image_scene: Hanuman calmly holding out his hands to be tied, demon soldiers around him looking confused.

title: No chair? Build one
story: Ravana's court gave him no seat. Hanuman coiled his tail into a tall spiral and sat on it, higher than Ravana's throne. No fuss. No shouting. Just a tail.
hit: If nobody pulls up a chair, make your own.
image_scene: Hanuman sitting on a tall coiled tower of his own tail, looking down at a startled Ravana.

title: Speak truth to a king
story: Standing before Ravana, Hanuman said: I am Ram's messenger. Return Sita and you will be forgiven. It was respectful and it was clear.
hit: Say the hard thing politely.
image_scene: Hanuman calmly addressing a crowned many-headed Ravana from a high coiled seat, courtiers silent.

title: A message can't be killed
story: Ravana wanted him executed. His brother Vibhishana spoke up: a messenger must not be killed. The court agreed to a lesser punishment: set his tail on fire.
hit: One steady voice can change the room.
image_scene: Vibhishana raising a hand in a hushed court, Hanuman standing wrapped in cloth behind him.

title: Oil on the tail
story: They wrapped cloth around his tail, soaked it in oil and lit it. They laughed. Hanuman waited quietly. The boon from Agni, years before, was still working.
hit: Preparation shows up in the funniest moments.
image_scene: Demon guards wrapping cloth around a long tail while Hanuman waits with calm closed eyes.

title: Lanka lights up
story: Flames on his tail, Hanuman jumped from roof to roof and set Lanka's palaces on fire, except the grove where Sita sat. A small fire, aimed well, changed a city.
hit: Precision beats force.
image_scene: Hanuman leaping across golden rooftops, a trail of orange fire behind him, Lanka at night.

title: The panic after the fire
story: Looking at the burning city, Hanuman suddenly feared he'd harmed Sita. He rushed back and found her safe, protected by her own faith. He had learned to check the damage.
hit: Own the impact, not just the intent.
image_scene: Hanuman running back anxiously toward the grove, relieved when Sita is seen safe and calm.

title: Cooling the tail
story: After the fire, Hanuman flew to the shore and dipped his burning tail in the sea. A small, funny moment between big ones. Even heroes need to cool down.
hit: Cool down before the next big thing.
image_scene: Hanuman holding the end of his tail in sparkling seawater, steam rising, small relieved smile.

title: The victory party at Madhuvan
story: On the way back, the vanaras reached Sugriva's honey grove, Madhuvan, and feasted without asking. They'd earned it. Sugriva guessed from the noise that the mission had succeeded.
hit: Celebrate wins, even before the full report.
image_scene: Happy vanaras eating honey and fruit in a lush grove, Hanuman laughing, Angada raising a cup.

title: Lead with the good news
story: When Hanuman reached Ram, his first words were: 'I have seen Sita.' Not a long story. Not a warm-up. The headline first, then the details.
hit: State the outcome first. Then explain.
image_scene: Hanuman bowing before Ram with joined hands, a glowing jewel in his palm, Ram's face lit with joy.

title: A bridge built together
story: Millions of vanaras, led by Nala and Neela, built a stone bridge across the sea. Hanuman carried, lifted and encouraged. No single hero built it. They all did.
hit: Big things are built by lots of small hands.
image_scene: Vanaras passing stones along a long bridge over the sea, Hanuman lifting a huge one.

title: Give them a second chance
story: When Ravana's brother Vibhishana asked to join Ram, many vanaras doubted him. Hanuman spoke up, saying he'd spoken honestly and acted with courage. Ram accepted him.
hit: People can switch sides when they find what's right.
image_scene: Vibhishana kneeling before Ram on the shore, Hanuman standing beside him gently supporting.

title: Ravana's compliment
story: In battle, Hanuman struck Ravana so hard that the demon king staggered. Ravana said: 'Well done, vanara. That was a great blow.' Even enemies recognise real strength.
hit: Respect your rival when they earn it.
image_scene: Hanuman with a raised fist facing a staggering Ravana, battlefield dust around them.

title: Lakshman falls
story: Indrajit's weapon struck Lakshman down. The camp went silent. The healer Sushena said only a herb from far Himalayan peaks could save him, and it had to be found before dawn.
hit: Some deadlines are not negotiable.
image_scene: Lakshman lying wounded as Ram kneels beside him, a tense dark-blue sky with a faint dawn line.

title: The longest night run
story: The healer asked Hanuman to fly north to Dronagiri mountain, bring four named herbs, and be back by sunrise. A journey of thousands of miles. He started instantly.
hit: Trust means someone hears 'impossible' and hears 'urgent'.
image_scene: Hanuman soaring through a starry night with snow-capped peaks below, determined face.

title: Kalanemi's trap
story: Ravana sent a demon, Kalanemi, disguised as a sage, to delay Hanuman. Hanuman was thirsty and almost fell for it, until a crocodile in a nearby pool revealed the truth.
hit: Be careful of 'help' that slows you down.
image_scene: A smiling fake sage offering a water pot to Hanuman beside a lake with a hidden crocodile.

title: Can't spot the herb? Bring the mountain
story: At Dronagiri, Hanuman couldn't tell which herbs were the right ones. So he lifted the whole mountain and flew it back. If you can't solve the small problem, solve the big one.
hit: Sometimes you carry the whole mountain.
image_scene: Hanuman flying with an entire glowing green mountain balanced on one palm across a night sky.

title: Bharat's accidental arrow
story: Passing over Nandigram, Bharat saw a huge shadow and shot an arrow at it. Hanuman fell, murmuring 'Ram, Ram'. Bharat rushed to help him, horrified, and Hanuman forgave instantly.
hit: Mistakes get fixed faster when both sides are kind.
image_scene: Bharat rushing forward to help Hanuman who is lying on grass, the mountain nearby still glowing.

title: Dawn delivered
story: Hanuman landed back before sunrise. Sushena prepared the herbs. Lakshman opened his eyes. Ram held Hanuman close and said no words were enough.
hit: Showing up on time can save a life.
image_scene: Dawn light breaking over the camp, Lakshman sitting up, Ram embracing Hanuman.

title: Ahiravana's kidnap
story: Ravana's relative Ahiravana, a sorcerer, kidnapped Ram and Lakshman and took them to Patala, the underworld. Hanuman went after them alone.
hit: When your people are in trouble, you go.
image_scene: Hanuman descending a dark spiral staircase into an underworld lit by glowing crystals.

title: A fortress made of tail
story: Before going to rescue them, Hanuman formed a protective fortress with his tail around the vanara camp so nothing could enter. Then he left, confident they were safe.
hit: A good leader builds safety before leaving.
image_scene: A giant coiled tail making a safe circular wall around a camp of sleeping vanaras at night.

title: Five faces, five flames
story: In Patala, five lamps in five directions had to be blown out at the same moment. Hanuman took the five-faced Panchamukhi form and extinguished them all at once.
hit: Some problems need every angle at the same time.
image_scene: Panchamukhi Hanuman with five calm faces facing five directions, five flames going out together.

title: Meeting his own son
story: In Patala, Hanuman met a guard named Makardhwaja, a being born from a drop of Hanuman's sweat. They fought without knowing. When they learned the truth, father and son embraced.
hit: Your own story can surprise you.
image_scene: A young fish-like guardian and Hanuman clasping hands, surprise melting into smiles.

title: Go and tell Bharat
story: As Ram's exile ended, he sent Hanuman ahead to tell Bharat that he was coming home. Bharat had vowed to give up his life if Ram didn't return on time. Hanuman arrived just in time.
hit: Some messages are urgent in the kindest way.
image_scene: Hanuman landing before Bharat at Nandigram with joined hands and a bright smile, Bharat in awe.

title: Why Hanuman is orange
story: Hanuman saw Sita put sindoor in her hair and asked why. 'For Ram's long life,' she said. He smeared sindoor all over his body to give Ram even more. That's why he is orange.
hit: Love can look a little over the top. It's still love.
image_scene: Hanuman covered head to toe in vermilion, Sita laughing gently, a small bowl of red powder beside him.

title: Pearls and an open heart
story: Sita gave Hanuman a pearl necklace. He bit each pearl and checked it. 'Where is Ram's name?' someone asked. He opened his chest and there, in his heart, were Ram and Sita.
hit: Show, don't tell.
image_scene: Hanuman with chest softly open showing glowing Ram and Sita, a pearl necklace in his hand.

title: The tail Bhima couldn't lift
story: In the Mahabharata, Bhima, famous for strength, found an old monkey blocking his path. He couldn't move its tail. The monkey was Hanuman, his half-brother in spirit, and Bhima's pride dissolved.
hit: Never judge by how someone looks.
image_scene: Bhima straining to lift an old monkey's tail, which barely moves, jungle path behind them.

title: The flag on Arjuna's chariot
story: At Kurukshetra, Arjuna's chariot carried a banner with Hanuman on it. According to tradition, Hanuman's presence protected the chariot throughout the war.
hit: Pick the logo you fight under.
image_scene: Arjuna's chariot with a saffron flag showing Hanuman, horses galloping across a golden field.

title: Arjuna's bridge of arrows
story: Arjuna once boasted he could build a bridge of arrows across the sea. Hanuman, disguised, said it would break under his weight. It did, until Krishna's help held it. Arjuna learned humility.
hit: Humble brag? Better to just ask for help.
image_scene: Hanuman stepping on a bridge of arrows over the sea while Arjuna watches, Krishna's hand under it.

title: Humbling Garuda
story: Krishna wanted to humble three proud people: Garuda, Satyabhama and his own Sudarshan. He called Hanuman in. By the end, the three had stopped competing.
hit: The loudest person in the room isn't the strongest.
image_scene: Hanuman sitting calmly in a palace garden while Garuda and Satyabhama look humbled.

title: Shani's challenge
story: Shani, the planet-god known for trouble, said he'd come to Hanuman. Hanuman invited him up and gave him a ride on his head, with a mountain on top. Shani promised never to trouble his devotees.
hit: Hard times can be handled with good humour.
image_scene: A tiny Shani trapped under a huge mountain on Hanuman's head, looking up apologetically.

title: Why Tuesday and Saturday
story: Tuesdays are linked with Mars (Mangal), and Saturdays with Shani, so those are the days many devotees keep for Hanuman. Some fast, some visit a temple, many just chant the Chalisa.
hit: A weekly habit beats a once-a-year push.
image_scene: A calendar with Tuesday and Saturday highlighted in soft orange, a tiny Hanuman standing on top.

title: Hanuman and Tulsidas
story: Tradition says Hanuman helped Tulsidas see Ram at Chitrakoot. After many failed attempts, a parrot-voiced hint changed everything. Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas and Chalisa in gratitude.
hit: The right nudge comes when you keep going.
image_scene: Sage Tulsidas writing on palm leaves by a river, Hanuman's gentle golden shadow behind him.

title: The Chalisa behind bars
story: A legend says Tulsidas was imprisoned by an emperor and sat chanting for forty days. Monkeys swarmed the palace and he was released. The poem he wrote is the Hanuman Chalisa.
hit: Pressure sometimes writes the best poetry.
image_scene: Tulsidas writing by a small window of a stone cell, tiny monkeys gathering outside the bars.

title: Sankat Mochan, Varanasi
story: In Varanasi, the Sankat Mochan temple is traditionally said to have been established by Tulsidas. The name means 'remover of troubles'. People walk there barefoot on Tuesdays and Saturdays.
hit: Some places turn into anchors for a whole city.
image_scene: A small orange temple gateway by the Ganga with a line of devotees at sunset.

title: He deleted his own masterpiece
story: In the Hanuman Nataka legend, Hanuman wrote his own Ramayana on rocks. When Valmiki saw it, he was sad because it overshadowed his. Hanuman threw the tablets into the sea.
hit: Real greatness doesn't need credit.
image_scene: Hanuman gently lowering large stone tablets into a calm sea while Valmiki watches with a soft smile.

title: Ram's name on every hair
story: A folk story says every hair on Hanuman's body says 'Ram'. When someone asked how deep his devotion went, he showed them, and the whole body hummed with the name.
hit: Do what you love so much it becomes you.
image_scene: Close-up of Hanuman's arm with tiny glowing Devanagari 'Ram' letters in each fine hair.

title: The ring in the underworld
story: Ram's ring slipped and fell into Patala. Hanuman followed and found thousands of identical rings. The king of Patala said: every Ram who has ever lived has dropped one. Hanuman understood how old this story is.
hit: Some stories repeat. That's how you know they matter.
image_scene: Hanuman holding one gold ring among thousands of identical rings in a glowing underground hall.

title: From India to Thailand to Java
story: Hanuman travels. In Thailand he is Hanuman in the Ramakien, in Java and Bali he is Hanoman in wayang shadow plays and Kecak dance. A story told across oceans.
hit: Stories pack light and go far.
image_scene: A world strip of Hanuman in three art styles: Indian, Thai, and Balinese, soft pastel backgrounds.

title: The wrestler's god
story: In northern India, akharas (wrestling pits) keep a Hanuman picture or shrine. Wrestlers touch the earth, bow to him and start practice. Strength with discipline.
hit: Start with a small ritual. It makes the rest easier.
image_scene: An akhara with clay floor and a small Hanuman shrine, a young wrestler bowing before training.

title: Sundara Kanda
story: The fifth book of the Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, is mostly Hanuman's journey to Lanka. Many families read it in tough times, as a story of courage when everything looks stuck.
hit: Courage can be a bedtime story.
image_scene: An open palm-leaf book glowing softly with a tiny Hanuman leaping out of it over a miniature sea.

title: The eleventh Rudra
story: In some traditions Hanuman is seen as an incarnation of Shiva, the eleventh of the Rudras. That's one reason many Shiva devotees also love him. Strength and stillness, together.
hit: Calm and powerful can be the same person.
image_scene: Hanuman meditating under a crescent moon, a faint trident shape of light behind him.

title: The Hanuman Ashtak
story: The Hanuman Ashtak, attributed to Tulsidas, has eight verses. Each begins with a famous moment, then asks 'who doesn't know your name, Sankat Mochan?' A reminder in a single breath.
hit: Short prayers are still prayers.
image_scene: Eight small floating diyas in an arc, each lighting a tiny scene of Hanuman, soft evening sky.

title: Hanuman Jayanti
story: Hanuman Jayanti marks his birth. Many celebrate on the full moon of Chaitra, though some regions celebrate on other days. Temples fill up with orange flowers, sindoor and chanting.
hit: A birthday doesn't need a cake to feel like a party.
image_scene: A temple courtyard lit by lamps, marigold garlands and a smiling baby Hanuman on a decorated seat.

title: Hanuman in Jain stories
story: In Jain tellings of the Ramayana, Hanuman is not a monkey but a prince of the vidyadharas, a skilled human race. The same hero, told differently, fits a different worldview.
hit: One person, many tellings.
image_scene: A regal young prince Hanuman with a tiny tail-shaped banner, in a Jain-style painted palace.

title: He out-sang Narada
story: Narada, the divine musician, grew proud of his veena. Hanuman sang. Rocks melted, the veena strings stuck in the soft stone, and Narada understood: skill isn't the same as depth.
hit: Don't confuse talent with soul.
image_scene: Hanuman singing peacefully beside a molten rock as Narada's veena stays embedded in it.

title: At Ram's feet
story: In every Ram Darbar picture, Hanuman sits at Ram's feet with folded hands, never at his side. The strongest figure in the scene takes the lowest seat, by choice.
hit: Position doesn't measure power.
image_scene: Ram Darbar scene with Ram, Sita and Lakshman seated and Hanuman kneeling at the front.

title: Where does he live now?
story: The Mahabharata says Hanuman lives on Gandhamadana mountain, a place of deep peace. Bhima's story shows him still around thousands of years after the Ramayana.
hit: Some people never stop being around.
image_scene: Hanuman sitting among lush Himalayan flowers on a mountain glowing in pastel light.

title: Forty verses, one prayer
story: 'Chalisa' comes from chalis, forty. The Hanuman Chalisa has forty chaupais, with two dohas at the beginning and one at the end. One short poem you can recite in a few minutes.
hit: Short can still be deep.
image_scene: An open book with forty tiny glowing lines of script, a small baby Hanuman sitting on its edge.

title: Written in Awadhi, for everyone
story: Tulsidas wrote it in Awadhi, a local language people actually spoke, not in Sanskrit. He wanted ordinary people to be able to say it themselves. Accessible by design.
hit: The best ideas speak the audience's language.
image_scene: Tulsidas writing with a quill while a crowd of simple villagers reads over his shoulder.

title: The distance to the sun, in one line
story: 'Jug sahastra jojan par bhanu.' Read as 12,000 x 1,000 x 8 miles, it comes to about 96 million miles, roughly 154 million km. The real distance is about 150 million km. Close.
hit: A line written long ago is surprisingly close to the answer.
image_scene: Baby Hanuman looking at a huge glowing sun and a measuring scroll marked with big numbers.

title: Bajrang: the thunderbolt body
story: 'Bajrang' comes from vajra-anga, a body like a thunderbolt. It points back to his childhood boon and the strength he shows in the verse 'Mahavir vikram Bajrangi'.
hit: A strong body is meant to serve something.
image_scene: Hanuman with a lightning-bolt pattern glowing through his arms, standing in a calm confident pose.

title: It starts with a guru, not a god
story: The first doha is about Tulsidas's guru. He says he cleans the mirror of his mind with the dust of his guru's feet. Before asking for strength, you clean the lens first.
hit: Start by cleaning the mirror.
image_scene: A hand wiping a hazy round mirror clean with a soft cloth, a clear sunny reflection emerging.

title: 'Give me strength, intellect, knowledge'
story: 'Bal buddhi vidya dehu mohi, harahu kalesh vikar.' The ask isn't for riches. It's for strength, intelligence and learning, and a request to remove troubles and flaws.
hit: Ask for capability, not just comfort.
image_scene: Baby Hanuman holding a glowing scroll, a dumbbell and a small lamp in his tiny hands.

title: Hard things become easy
story: 'Durgam kaaj jagat ke jete, sugam anugraha tumhre tete.' All the difficult tasks in the world become easy through your grace. A line for people with a big to-do list.
hit: Hard is often just 'unfamiliar'.
image_scene: A mountain path with steps appearing one by one under Hanuman's feet in soft golden light.

title: Gatekeeper of Ram's door
story: 'Ram duare tum rakhvare.' You are the guard at Ram's door; no one enters without your permission. Hanuman as gatekeeper, a reminder to be careful what you let in.
hit: Protect your peace. Choose what comes in.
image_scene: Hanuman standing guard at a golden doorway, a gentle hand held out like a polite 'wait here'.

title: 'Why fear when you are the protector?'
story: 'Tum rakshak kahu ko darna.' When you have a protector, why be afraid? Not a line about having no problems. A line about having somewhere to put your fear.
hit: You are allowed to lean on something.
image_scene: Small child behind a calm giant Hanuman who holds a mace gently, peaceful night sky behind.

title: Align thought, word, deed
story: 'Sankat te Hanuman chhudave, man kram vachan dhyan jo lave.' Hanuman frees one from trouble when mind, action and word are all aligned. Three things, pointing the same way.
hit: Say it, do it, think it. Same direction.
image_scene: Three arrows of light labelled mind, word, deed pointing in the same direction beside Hanuman.

title: Only you can hold your own power
story: 'Aapan tej samhaaro aapai, teenon lok haank te kaanpai.' You alone can hold your own radiance; the three worlds tremble at your call. Power needs control.
hit: Self-control is the real flex.
image_scene: Hanuman gently cupping a glowing orb of light between both hands, calm face.

title: The fear verse
story: 'Bhoot pishach nikat nahin aave, Mahavir jab naam sunave.' Evil spirits don't come near when the great hero's name is spoken. Many people say this line when they feel scared at night.
hit: A name or a phrase can be a flashlight.
image_scene: A child holding a lit diya in a dark corridor, a soft Hanuman glow growing behind them.

title: Seven times or a hundred?
story: Verse 38 says 'jo sat baar paath kar koi', whoever recites this 'sat baar'. Most read it as a hundred times. Some read it as seven. The Chalisa leaves that to you.
hit: A routine is yours to define.
image_scene: Two small mala bead strings, one short and one long, held in Hanuman's hands, gentle smile.

title: Shiva as witness
story: 'Jo yah padhe Hanuman Chalisa, hoy siddhi saakhi Gaureesa.' Whoever reads it, success follows, and Gaureesa, Shiva, is the witness. The poem ends by naming a witness, not a guarantee.
hit: A promise feels different with a witness.
image_scene: A tiny Shiva with a crescent moon watching from a distance as Hanuman reads from a scroll.

title: Tulsidas signs off humbly
story: 'Tulsidas sada Hari chera, keejai Nath hriday mah dera.' Tulsidas calls himself Hari's servant and asks Hanuman to live in his heart. The author's whole signature.
hit: End with humility.
image_scene: Tulsidas with folded hands, a small glowing Hanuman figure resting in the centre of his chest.

title: The closing doha
story: 'Pavan tanay sankat harana, mangal moorati roop.' Son of the wind, remover of troubles, form of auspiciousness. Then a request: stay in my heart, with Ram, Lakshman and Sita.
hit: A good ending is a request to stay.
image_scene: Hanuman sitting gently with Ram, Lakshman and Sita as tiny figures glowing inside his heart.

title: Siyavar Ramchandra ki jai
story: The Jaikara is the cheer at the end: 'Siyavar Ramchandra ki jai, Pavansut Hanuman ki jai'. A shout of joy that turns a prayer into a celebration.
hit: Finish loud. Joy counts.
image_scene: Hanuman with both arms raised in a happy cheer, orange petals and sparks in the air.

title: Why 108?
story: 108 is traditionally treated as sacred: a mala has 108 beads, and many mantras are repeated 108 times. This Feed has 108 stories so you can walk through one bead at a time.
hit: One bead at a time is still a full mala.
image_scene: A glowing 108-bead mala forming a circle, Hanuman at the centre touching the first bead.
